correctness.rationale: Each rank-one matrix with total sum 1 has a unique factorization u v^T with sum u=sum v=1. Splitting those affine hyperplanes reduces each Fourier multiplier to a bilinear sum over d=m-1,e=n-1. Summation over x then y gives nonzero q^(d+e-r) times a pth-root phase precisely when ell in im B and h in im B^T; for rank r, each admissible linear term has q^r choices and scalar constant c has q choices. Thus multiplicity q^(2r+1)N_de(r), with phases equally distributed. The rank-deficit distribution derived from the exact matrix-rank product and dominated convergence gives the sequential rectangular limit, not a joint uniform estimate. Independent full character enumeration at q=2 and dimensions 2x2,2x3,3x2,3x3 agrees including zeros. The proof (not enumeration) covers all finite fields.
